meta.title: Internet Speed Test - Free Online Connection Checker
meta.description: Test your internet speed for free. Check download speed, upload speed, and ping instantly.
meta.subtitle: Test your internet connection speed instantly

content.p1: Test your internet connection speed with our free, accurate speed test tool. Measure your download speed, upload speed, and ping latency in seconds. Perfect for troubleshooting slow connections, verifying ISP speeds, or checking if you're getting what you pay for.
req_list: Close all other applications and browser tabs
Connect via Ethernet cable for most accurate results
Disable VPN or proxy services temporarily
Ensure no downloads or uploads are running
Test multiple times at different times of day
why_list: Verify you're getting the speed you're paying for
Compare different ISP plans before switching
Document speed for ISP support tickets
improve_list: Use Ethernet cable instead of Wi-Fi when possible
Place router in central location away from walls
Upgrade to a modern router that supports your speed tier
Use Quality of Service (QoS) settings on router
tips_list: Test at different times of day to see variations
Run multiple tests and average the results
Test on different devices to rule out device issues
Compare Wi-Fi speeds at different locations in your home

download.title: Download Speed
download.desc: How fast data travels from the internet to your device. Important for streaming, browsing, and downloading files.

upload.title: Upload Speed
upload.desc: How fast data travels from your device to the internet. Important for video calls, uploading files, and live streaming.

ping.title: Ping (Latency)
ping.desc: Response time of your connection. Lower is better. Important for gaming and real-time applications.

congestion.title: Network Congestion
congestion.desc: Peak usage times can slow down your connection as more users share bandwidth.

wifi.title: Wi-Fi Signal
wifi.desc: Distance from router, walls, and interference from other devices affect wireless speeds.

device.title: Device Performance
device.desc: Older devices or those running many programs may not achieve full speeds.

router.title: Router Quality
router.desc: Outdated routers may not support your full internet speed capabilities.

faq.q1: What is a good internet speed?
faq.a1: For general browsing and streaming: 25+ Mbps. For 4K streaming and gaming: 50+ Mbps. For multiple users and heavy usage: 100+ Mbps. For remote work and large households: 200+ Mbps.
faq.q2: Why is my speed slower than advertised?
faq.a2: ISPs advertise "up to" speeds. Actual speeds depend on network congestion, Wi-Fi quality, distance from router, and device capabilities. Test with Ethernet for most accurate results.
faq.q3: What's the difference between Mbps and MBps?
faq.a3: Mbps (megabits per second) is used for internet speeds. MBps (megabytes per second) is used for file sizes. 1 MBps = 8 Mbps. A 100 Mbps connection downloads at about 12.5 MBps.
faq.q4: How accurate is this speed test?
faq.a4: Our speed test provides accurate results by measuring real data transfer. For best accuracy, close other applications, use Ethernet, and run multiple tests.
faq.q5: Should I test with Wi-Fi or Ethernet?
faq.a5: Test with Ethernet to measure your true internet speed. Test with Wi-Fi to diagnose wireless issues. Comparing both helps identify if problems are with your internet or Wi-Fi.
